Today marked my last day as a Cloud, Data, and AI Intern at PwC ! Over the past few months, I have had the opportunity to get hands-on with spatial data modelling and agentic architecture. A few highlights from the summer: • I implemented a density-based clustering algorithm to map and analyze large-scale regional incident data, identifying spatial hotspots for resource deployment optimization. • I attended TMLS - Toronto Machine Learning Summit , where I connected with ML practitioners, researchers, and executives to learn about the cutting-edge work being deployed across the industry. Talks and workshop topics included long-context training, foundation models, and reinforcement learning. • I developed a comprehensive benchmark comparing an internal SDK against standard agentic systems, which demonstrated up to a 26% F1 improvement and quantified the specific efficiency trade-offs of these systems. A massive thank you to Shiva Sathia , Ryan Barnhart , Melika Vahdat , and Andrew F. for the support over the summer, and I’m incredibly grateful to everyone else I had the pleasure of connecting with along the way. Excited for what’s next!

TraceRoot.AI (YC S25) now natively traces pi-mono! A few weeks ago Databricks benchmarked coding agents on their own multi-million-line codebase. The surprise winner on cost-efficiency: pi — the minimal, white-box harness from Mario Zechner . Running the same models, it matched the vendor harnesses (Claude Code / Codex) on quality at up to 2× lower cost per task — mostly because it feeds the model ~3× less context per turn: a tighter working set, fewer runs. Honestly, I've been recommending pi to my founder friends for a while now: it's minimal, fully customizable (the whole harness is yours to edit), and you adapt it to your workflow instead of the other way around. If you're building agents, it's worth a serious look. And the moment you host one in your product, observability stops being optional. And now you can see exactly what a pi run is doing with traceroot! 1. CLI extension → if you run pi as a coding agent `pi install npm:@traceroot-ai/pi-extension` Every pi run you kick off from the terminal gets traced automatically — conversation turns, LLM calls, tool executions, cost, tokens. 2. pi SDK wrapper (v0.1.8) → if you build on pi inside your own product When pi is the engine behind your customer-facing agent, wire it in with a few lines: `TraceRoot.initialize({ instrumentModules: { piCodingAgent: pi } })` Traces flow straight to our cloud platform — into CI or any automations. Same rich output either way: per-query traces, planning → every tool call → final output, with the token count on each step — so you can watch where your context budget goes, and see for yourself why pi is so lean. Open source, free tier, a few lines to get going. - pi extension: https://lnkd.in/eMCdkp7W - SDK (v0.1.8): https://lnkd.in/eVnMcV4u Give it a try! 👉 app.traceroot.ai

TraceRoot.AI (YC S25) now has dashboards, purpose-built for AI agents! 📊 Individual traces are perfect for deep dives. But when you want the big picture — latency, cost, tokens, and error rate across all your agents over time — aggregated metrics just belong in a dashboard. So we built one. What's in Dashboard v1: - A seeded Overview dashboard out of the box, so you're never staring at a blank page - A widget builder with live preview — build the charts you want and watch them render as you go - Time-series charts with percentiles, averages, counts, and category breakdowns, over any time range - A trace-feed widget where every row clicks straight through to the actual trace behind the number Coming soon: - Pull your dashboard's aggregated metrics straight from the CLI 🖥️ - Create persistent dashboards from the CLI instead of the UI stay tuned~ 👉 app.traceroot.ai
